claims.text: Don't assume a psychiatric cause or intoxication, even with a known psychiatric diagnosis or an odor of alcohol.
claims.quote: Do not assume that the cause or the only cause of abnormal behavior is a psychiatric disorder or intoxication, even in patients who have a known psychiatric diagnosis or an odor of alcohol.

claims.text: Vital signs and blood tests once the patient is safely controlled, to find the cause.
claims.quote: Such interventions are done to prevent harm to patients and others and to allow evaluation of the cause of the behavior (eg, by taking vital signs and doing blood tests).

claims.text: Fingerstick glucose and pulse oximetry: a patient with a known psychiatric disorder, typical symptoms, normal mental status, normal exam and vitals, normal pulse oximetry and normal fingerstick glucose usually needs no further labs.
claims.quote: Patients with a known psychiatric disorder who have an exacerbation of their typical symptoms and no new physical symptoms, a normal mental status, normal physical examination (including vital signs and pulse oximetry), and normal fingerstick glucose testing, do not typically require further laboratory testing.

claims.text: Toxicology screen (urine drug screen, blood alcohol level) with recent substance use or signs of intoxication.
claims.quote: Toxicology screening (eg, urine drug screen, blood alcohol level) is done if the patient has a recent history of substance use disorder or physical signs suggesting intoxication or recent substance use (eg, needle marks).
